pos.personaBrief: No verified evidence on possession (gap axis); from general knowledge, Ferguson's sides controlled the ball at Old Trafford but were most lethal breaking at pace (1999 and 2007-08 counters), consistent with the verified attacking use of wingers.

pro.personaBrief: No verified evidence on build-up (gap axis); from general knowledge, United played forward quickly and went long when needed, though Scholes and Carrick were valued for passes that broke lines, which fits the verified 'more attacking alternative' signing of Kanchelskis.

est.personaBrief: No verified evidence on structure (gap axis); from general knowledge, a disciplined 4-4-2 with clear roles (in line with the verified wide wingers), but with forwards like Cantona and Rooney dropping off and Giggs/Ronaldo free to drift inside.

lar.personaBrief: Verified: Kanchelskis signed for the right wing (1991) and Giggs and Blomqvist used wide in 1998-99 'to prevent the opposition from playing narrow', so the flanks were central to his attacking idea.

blo.personaBrief: No verified evidence on the block (gap axis); from general knowledge, United defended in an aggressive mid-block, with forwards working hard and quick pressure after losing the ball, without being a pure pressing side.

mar.personaBrief: No verified evidence on marking (gap axis, openQuestions); from general knowledge, a zonal back four in open play, man-marking at set pieces, and occasional dedicated markers on stars (Park on Pirlo in 2010).

pla.personaBrief: No verified evidence on game plan (gap axis); from general knowledge, Ferguson kept an attacking identity domestically but was pragmatic in Europe, changing shape and making aggressive in-game changes to chase results.

res.personaBrief: No verified evidence on purpose (gap axis); from general knowledge, winning was everything to Ferguson, but United's tradition was to keep attacking and go for goals late rather than shut games down.

sis.personaBrief: No verified evidence on system vs talent (gap axis); from general knowledge, Ferguson relied on great players and gave Cantona and Ronaldo freedom and licence to dribble, while demanding work rate from everyone, consistent with the verified emphasis on players believing in him.

jog.personaBrief: No verified evidence on player type (gap axis); from general knowledge, he prized pace, power and stamina (Keane, Ronaldo, Rooney, the verified fast wingers) and struggled to fit slow playmakers like Veron.

bas.personaBrief: Verified: 'often credited for valuing youth' at United in the 1990s; the Class of 92 became title-winning starters early, alongside signings.

lid.personaBrief: Verified: a 'siege mentality' at Aberdeen and 'I finally had the players believing in me' show a manager who built unity through his own authority; he ran the dressing room himself and no star was above him.
